title: why my fire number is 666k
excerpt: how I calculated my target net worth to FIRE and live comfortably.
body:
A lot of people looking into retiring early usually aim high, with 2 million and above as their goal. (I know because I stalk the subreddit)

Those numbers make sense for those planning to retire:
- in HCOL (high cost of living) cities
- support a large family
- or live lavishly with first-class flights, star-rated meals, and the ability to spend money as you please

I don't aim so high.. 

This journey that I have embarked on is to retire in Taiwan comfortably. I will travel a few times a year and work as I choose to.
And I would effectively coastFIRE until my retirement age after working a couple of years in the US.

Assuming the portfolio earns an average return of 7%, and inflation averages 3%, that $666,000 could grow to roughly $3.16 million in future dollars, or about $1.6 million in today’s purchasing power, without any additional investments.

That would support annual spending of approximately $40,000 to $60,000 at a withdrawal rate of roughly 2.5% to 3.75%.

If you just got to know FIRE and want to calculate your FIRE number, I have a guide on calculating your retirement number here.

PS. Time may change my retirement plans; however, this is as of rn
